comment: Single source of truth for every MimOS runtime colour.
The canonical five are normative and come from docs/BRAND.md; they must
not be edited without a brand decision. Theme roles may derive new tints
from them, but every derived value must state why it is not canonical.
scripts/generate-color-schemes.py turns this file into Plasma colour
schemes and refuses to emit a theme whose text pairs fail WCAG AA.

besito.purpose: Hearts, the OS letters, and highlights

mimos-claro.name: MimOS Claro
mimos-claro.description: Daytime scheme on Nube with Noche text and Abrazo accents.

derivations.selectionBackground: Abrazo darkened to #5B3BE0 so white selection text reaches AA on a light surface; #7C5CFC does not.
derivations.positive: Calma is a 1.9:1 pair on white and cannot carry text at all; darkened to #136B5B, a teal of the same hue that reaches AA on both light surfaces.
derivations.negative: Besito is decorative and fails as light-surface text; deepened to #B0123F, a red-pink of the same family.
derivations.neutral: Amber #7A5200 has no canonical entry; chosen because no canonical colour reaches AA as a warning on both the window and view surfaces.
derivations.windowBackgroundAlternate: A desktop needs at least three separable surfaces and the palette defines one light background. Nube tinted toward Abrazo gives #EDE7FA, the raised surface used by buttons, headers, and inactive titles.
derivations.viewBackgroundAlternate: Alternating list rows need a step smaller than the window step, so Nube is tinted only slightly toward Abrazo to give #F5F1FE.
derivations.hoverDecoration: Hover must be visible without reading as focus or selection, so Abrazo is lightened to #9B86FF. It is decoration only and carries no text, so it is exempt from the AA text pairs.

mimos-oscuro.name: MimOS Oscuro
mimos-oscuro.description: Night scheme on Noche with Nube text and lifted Abrazo accents.

derivations.link: Abrazo is a 3.4:1 pair on Noche and cannot carry body text; lifted to #B3A2FF at the same hue.
derivations.negative: Besito is decorative; lifted to #FF9AB4 so error text reaches AA on both dark surfaces.
derivations.focusDecoration: Calma marks focus because it is the only canonical colour that separates clearly from Abrazo selection.
derivations.windowBackgroundAlternate: Noche lifted one step to #2C2444 for the raised surface used by buttons, headers, tooltips, and active titles. The palette defines one dark background and a desktop needs a hierarchy.
derivations.viewBackground: Noche lowered one step to #1A1430 so text views recede behind window chrome, which is the usual Plasma relationship.
derivations.hoverDecoration: Hover must be visible without reading as focus or selection, so Abrazo is lightened to #9B86FF. It is decoration only and carries no text, so it is exempt from the AA text pairs.
derivations.selectionBackground: Measured: white on canonical Abrazo #7C5CFC is 4.38:1, just under AA, so Abrazo cannot carry white text at any size. Neither can Noche sit on it (3.70:1). Abrazo is therefore darkened to #7452F5, which reaches 5.03:1 with white while staying 3.27:1 against the window background. This limit applies anywhere Abrazo is used as a filled button; it is a property of the canonical colour, not of this theme.
derivations.surfaceRaised: Noche lifted two steps to #3A3058. The MimOS applications draw cards inside an already raised panel and need a third dark surface; windowBackgroundAlternate is the second. Carries no text of its own.

mimos-nocturnos.name: Mimos nocturnos
mimos-nocturnos.description: Late-night scheme: warmer, dimmer, and lower in blue than MimOS Oscuro, without dropping any text pair below AA.

derivations.windowForeground: Nube is a cool white; replaced with the warm off-white #EFE3DA so the scheme emits less blue at night. Still AA on every surface. Reused by the active title bar.
derivations.windowBackground: Noche shifted warm and slightly darker to #1C1622; the hue moves toward red so the whole scheme reads warmer. Reused by the inactive title bar.
derivations.positive: Calma desaturated and warmed to #8CC7B6 so it sits inside this scheme instead of glowing against it.
derivations.selectionBackground: Abrazo desaturated; full-strength Abrazo is the brightest element on screen and defeats the purpose of a night scheme.
derivations.selectionForeground: Nube is a cool white and would reintroduce the blue this scheme exists to reduce; warmed to #FDF6F0 to match the body text.
derivations.windowBackgroundAlternate: The warmed Noche lifted one step to #251E2D for the raised surface used by buttons, headers, tooltips, and active titles.
derivations.viewBackground: The warmed Noche lowered one step to #15111A so text views recede behind window chrome.
derivations.negative: Besito warmed and dimmed to #F2A0A8. Full Besito is the loudest colour in the palette, and an error message at night should be readable, not startling.
derivations.hoverDecoration: Hover must be visible without reading as focus or selection, so Abrazo is lightened to #9B86FF. It is decoration only and carries no text, so it is exempt from the AA text pairs.

contrastRequirements.comment: Minimum WCAG ratios enforced for every theme by the generator.

acceptedLogotypeContrast.OS: Besito OS measures 2.38:1 on Nube. WCAG 1.4.3 exempts logotypes, the letters are set at 112-190px so legibility is not in question, and docs/BRAND.md forbids recolouring the masters. OS is an accent on a name whose legibility is carried by Mim at 15.07:1, so the low ratio is accepted rather than corrected. This exemption covers the logotype only; it must never be used to justify Besito as body text.

mimos-logo-banner.svg.intent: self-contained banner; carries its own Noche background so it is independent of the page theme

mimos-logo-horizontal-dark-no-tagline.sv.rationale: The installer sidebar is Abrazo-dark #5B3BE0, which is neither of the two surfaces the existing horizontal masters declare. The light master is unusable there: it contains #5B3BE0 itself, so part of it measures exactly 1.00:1 and disappears. The dark master is readable except for its tagline, set in #B3A2FF, which measures 3.03:1 -- below the 4.5:1 this project requires of prose. No lockup pairing the heart with the wordmark exists without a tagline, and BRAND.md forbids rearranging a master, so this is a new master approved by David rather than an edit of an existing one. Every element keeps the geometry and fill it has in the dark master; only the tagline is absent and the canvas is narrowed from 1200 to 979 to match the content, preserving the source's 107-unit right margin.

acceptedLogotypeContrast.OS: Besito OS measures 2.59:1 on #5B3BE0. WCAG 1.4.3 exempts logotypes, the letters are set at 112px, and Mim carries the name's legibility at 6.16:1. Same exemption as the light masters record on Nube; it covers the logotype only and never justifies Besito as body text.

logoSurfacesComment: Every lockup declares the surface it is drawn for. #0D1117 is GitHub's dark canvas, the darkest surface MimOS artwork is placed on, so passing there passes on Noche too. scripts/check-logo-contrast.py measures the real fills in the SVG against these values and fails if prose drops below 4.5:1 or if the wordmark's emphasis inverts between surfaces.

appTokens.comment: The token block the Qt/QML application declares. Generated into Main.qml between the mimos-palette markers so the application, the desktop schemes, and the artwork all resolve to one palette. Two applications used to declare it and disagreed; the installer prototype has since been removed, and Calamares takes its colours from packages/mimos-calamares-config/branding.desc instead. A value is either a role of the named theme or 'canonical:<name>'. The application is a branded dark surface regardless of which desktop scheme the user selects.

fontsComment: Fonts the brand SVGs are allowed to name. It is empty, and that is now the point: every packaged lockup has its glyphs outlined by scripts/generate-brand-lockups.py, so no asset names a family and there is nothing left to resolve at runtime. That closes a class of defect this project hit twice. First the assets declared 'Inter, Montserrat, system-ui, sans-serif' and QtSvg handed the whole chain to QFont, which takes one family name, so it matched nothing (ADR-047). Then Baloo 2 was named plainly and Pango read it as the family Baloo at size 2 -- its font descriptions are 'Family Style Size' -- and rendered the wordmark in DejaVu Serif, byte-identical to asking for DejaVu Serif outright. Quoting fixes one renderer and breaks the other; outlining removes the question. check-brand-fonts.py still runs and now enforces the stronger invariant: a packaged brand asset may name no font at all. The vendor production files under branding/merch/apparel were always outlined, for the same reason.
